angles.title: What one street does at 3 AM: ovens, bins and a fox
angles.summary: The night timeline of Kettle Lane, minute by minute, told through what the camera found: the street is busy, just not with us.
angles.hook: I photographed one street at 3 AM for six weeks. It is louder than at noon.
angles.audience: Anyone who has walked home late; street photographers

evidence.claim: The bakery switches on its ovens at about 3:10 AM
Bins go out at 3:40 AM and the street is loud for eleven minutes
A fox crossed near number 27 on 31 of the 42 nights

angles.why: It is the most showable fact in the project and it carries the thesis argument without saying 'thesis'.

angles.title: Three rules that shaped the whole thesis
angles.summary: Same route, available light only, no staging: how three constraints set before night one decided the work, and which rule cost the most.
angles.hook: Before the first night I wrote three rules. One cost me most of my frames.

evidence.claim: Chapter 1 sets three rules before the first night
Rule 3 gave the author the best frames

angles.why: Constraints are a lesson any creative reader can steal, and the voice is good at honest trade-offs.

angles.title: Sodium lamps vs film: why I switched in week three
angles.summary: Every roll came out orange under sodium lamps; the switch to digital at a fixed 2800K white balance, and what it says about choosing the tool for the light.
angles.hook: Two weeks of film. Every roll came out orange.

evidence.claim: Switched from film to digital in week three because sodium lamps turned every roll orange
White balance set by hand to 2800K for the rest of the project

angles.why: Specific, slightly technical and self-deprecating: exactly how the README already talks.

angles.title: 2,100 exposures, 48 frames: editing is the real work
angles.summary: What it takes to cut 2,100 exposures down to 48, and why the edit is where a body of work actually gets its point.
angles.audience: Photographers and creatives building a portfolio

evidence.claim: 2,100 exposures in total, 48 made the final edit

angles.why: A number that stops the scroll and a lesson about editing that travels beyond photography.

angles.title: Only 9 people walked the whole street in six weeks
angles.summary: Who actually uses a street at night: 9 walkers, the bakers, the bin crew and a fox; a short data-driven post on the thesis argument.
angles.hook: In six weeks of nights, 9 people walked the whole street. A fox crossed it on 31 nights.

evidence.claim: Only 9 people walked the full length of the street in six weeks
A fox crossed near number 27 on 31 of the 42 nights

angles.why: Counts from the author's own log make a playful but true contrast.

recommended: What one street does at 3 AM: ovens, bins and a fox
recommendation_reason: It is the strongest visual story, it fits the two platforms where this project lands best (Instagram and TikTok), and every beat is a logged time from the findings chapter. It also leads naturally into the graduate show.
